newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: UBS buys 26 pct stake in Daewoo Motor.
newsitem.headline: UBS buys 26 pct stake in Daewoo Motor.

text.p: The Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) bought a 26 percent stake, or 18.45 million shares, in Daewoo Motor Co, a carmaking unit of South Korea's Daewoo Group, a Daewoo spokesman said on Friday.

UBS bought the stake through its Malaysian subsidiary Artec Ltd for $200 million, becoming the third largest shareholder and the only foreign shareholder. Purchase of the shares was completed in June, a company statement said.

Daewoo Corp's 50 percent stake in the company has now been reduced to 37 percent, but it is still the largest shareholder. Daewoo Electronics is the second largest shareholder with a 28.5 percent stake, down from 38.6 percent before the UBS purchase.
Most of the other shares are owned by Daewoo units and corporate executives.

Daewoo Motor's paid-in capital had been enlarged to 354.67 billion won from 262.44 billion. This would help Daewoo finance huge investment in new auto production plant in South Korean city of Kunsan, the statement said.
The Kunsan plant now under construction will boost Daewoo's annual domestic car production capacity by 300,000 to more than one million.
South Korea's third largest carmaker severed an unhappy 15-year marriage with U.S. auto giant General Motors (GM) in 1993 following disputes over sales and investment strategy.
The company earlier said it would invest $6 billion in overseas plants in the next two to three years to meet its ambition to be a big player in the world car industry.
Daewoo Motor last year took over major stakes in Polish carmakers Fabryka Samochodow Osobowych (FSO) and Fabryka Samochodow Lublinie.
The company has major production bases in Uzbekistan, the Czech Republic, Romania and India. It has smaller plants in the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia and Iran.
